title: fix(sessions): distinguish slow database holders from queued writers
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Slow database reservations outside the session-write wrapper can leave operators with queue delays but no corresponding holder diagnostic. Session-write warnings also lose their structured timing fields in diagnostic events.

## User Impact

Operators can distinguish a settled reservation held for at least one second from a fast write that merely waited in the queue. The diagnostic reports fixed direct, worker, or ordered-read categories; it does not identify a unique request or claim that the hold was SQL execution.

## Why This Change Was Made

Observe the existing admission owner without changing FIFO, reentrancy, cancellation, or accepted-work settlement. Skip duplicate observations when the session wrapper owns timing, mark its reentrant writes, and preserve structured fields in both diagnostic events and file logs. The new reservation diagnostic contains no paths, session identifiers, payloads, or error text. Occupancy includes awaited work and is reported only after settlement; ordered reads across multiple stores can report multiple reservations. This adds diagnosis, not a latency cure. A separate follow-up remains for the existing message-first archive-pruning warnings in `session-history-archive-pruning-diagnostics.ts`; this change preserves their current file-log consumers.

## Evidence

- Independent source review and autoreview completed. The actionable logger argument-order finding was corrected with real transport regression coverage.
- Baseline `ba6d0131bd6df7114b23b673853da1bde6205ff5` with the candidate tests reproduced four failures: two missing holder warnings and two session diagnostic events missing their timing fields. These were behavioral assertion failures, not setup failures.
- Runtime executed on `9cf9d3cf9bd6e2a53f7f930096f5bc60414930ac`: **59/59 passed** across admission, session scope, the unchanged writer queue, writer ownership, reclamation, and cleanup. This includes real SQLite work, real diagnostic transport/file metadata, cancellation, reentrancy, privacy, and original settlement identity.
- Final signed head `3f0f8fcd6cef171e3bff513a4df79dc65c4f35c1` differs only by explicit `unknown` types on a test logger callback and a documented lint exception for the deliberate non-Error rejection fixture. Production and every test runtime expression/assertion are unchanged; the 59-test receipt is carried forward on that basis, not presented as a new execution.
- Changed-surface validation is complete: production types, all 27 selected test type graphs, formatting, scoped lint, ratchets, dead exports, import cycles, schema/storage and remaining planned guards passed. The first run exposed the test callback overload inference; after its correction, the failed and three unfinished graphs passed. The lint fixture comment resolved the only scoped lint failure. Previously passing checks were retained; only failed or unfinished checks ran again. `git diff --check` passed.
- Proof used a trusted native PR checkout with its own frozen install on Node 26.7.0 / pnpm 12.5.1 / macOS arm64 after the remote proof lease expired in its queue. The final proof tree matches the signed head exactly. The pinned tslog 5.2.0 source/types and OpenClaw transport contract were inspected directly.
- Production delta is +72 lines, justified by observation at the existing reservation owner and preserved structured logging; tests/support add 405 net lines. No queue, schema, config, protocol, or SDK contract changes. The latest exact-head review has no code or security findings; its remaining test-cost reporting request is answered below. Final security aggregation remains a separate enforced landing gate.

- Exact-head single-worker cost, measured on `3f0f8fcd6cef171e3bff513a4df79dc65c4f35c1` with `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <file> --maxWorkers=1` (the trusted-checkout repository wrapper): `src/state/openclaw-agent-write-admission.test.ts` **9/9 passed, 1.935 s command wall** (0.805 s Vitest); `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-scope.test.ts` **7/7 passed, 8.304 s command wall** (6.64 s Vitest, including 3.321 s reused compiled-worker preparation). These are fresh executions at the signed head, measured separately with a monotonic clock; cached test-body durations are not used as wall time. No real-time delay was added to either test.
- Hosted [CI run 37817697829](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37817697829) passed at the same head: **684 s elapsed**, from 17:35:06 to 17:46:30 UTC, including all selected jobs (not per-file test time). Its CI gate and security-fast job passed. The follow-on Security Review run is [37819164727](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37819164727); native landing still enforces its aggregate result.
